question: Simplify \(\sin(x-y)\cos y\)\({}+\cos(x-y)\sin y.\)
solution:
The two products have the form of the sine addition formula:
\[
\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v.
\]
Combining the angles is useful because \((x-y)+y=x\). Taking \(u=x-y\) and \(v=y\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x-y)\cos y+\cos(x-y)\sin y
&=\sin((x-y)+y)\\
&=\boxed{\sin x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This identity holds for all real angles \(x\) and \(y\). The answer is choice B.
